scope: Reference constants for the Phase-2 geometric radio model (radio_model="geometric"). No Phase-0 dataset carries an RSSI/path-loss observable, so nothing here is scored yet -- these entries exist so the Phase-2 implementation and its unit tests grade against ONE audited copy of the constants.

urban_los.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0, 'Study on evaluation methodology of new Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) use cases for LTE and NR', V2V channel models (Table 6.2.1-1): Urban LOS PL = 38.77 + 16.7*log10(d_3D) + 18.2*log10(fc_GHz). Transcribed independently in docs/realism/ROADMAP.md section 3.2 item 1, in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md, and in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(a) (which cross-checked it against the ns-3 ThreeGppV2vUrbanPropagationLossModel source); all three agree.
urban_los.note: d in metres (TR 37.885 uses 3-D distance; the Phase-2 model is 2-D + antenna heights), fc in GHz.

urban_nlos.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 Table 6.2.1-1, Urban NLOS (building-blocked, 'NLOSb' in GEMV2 vocabulary): PL = 36.85 + 30*log10(d_3D) + 18.9*log10(fc_GHz). Same three-way agreement as urban_los (ROADMAP section 3.2 item 1, PHASE2-DESIGN.md, research-net-sota.json section 2(a) verified against the ns-3 implementation).
urban_nlos.note: d in metres, fc in GHz. Distance exponent 3.0 -- this state decays far faster than LOS and is what makes the urban gray zone narrow (see nlos_link_budget_consequence_m).

highway_los.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 Table 6.2.1-1, Highway LOS: PL = 32.4 + 20*log10(d_3D) + 20*log10(fc_GHz). Highway NLOS/NLOSv reuse the urban formulas (research-net-sota.json section 2(a): 'NLOS/NLOSv reuse urban formulas'). Same three-way agreement as urban_los.
highway_los.note: d in metres, fc in GHz. This is the free-space form to within 0.0478 dB -- see highway_los_free_space_offset_db before substituting an exact FSPL implementation.

highway_los_free_space_offset_db.cite: derived from the Friis free-space constant vs TR 37.885 highway LOS
highway_los_free_space_offset_db.source: Exact free-space path loss with d in metres and fc in GHz is PL = 32.447783 + 20*log10(d) + 20*log10(fc), where 32.447783 = 20*log10(4*pi*1e9/299792458). TR 37.885's highway LOS intercept is 32.4, i.e. the standard's rounded intercept sits 0.047783 dB BELOW exact free space. Computed here at full double precision on 2026-08-30.
highway_los_free_space_offset_db.note: IMPLEMENTER TRAP: the Phase-2 gate is 'match published constants to 0.01 dB'. An implementation that reuses a generic Friis/FSPL helper for highway LOS is wrong by 0.048 dB at EVERY distance and fails that gate by ~5x. Use the literal 32.4 intercept.

pathloss_at_reference_distances_db.unit: [state, distance m, path loss dB at fc = 5.9 GHz]
pathloss_at_reference_distances_db.cite: TR 37.885 constants evaluated at the ROADMAP Phase-2 gate distances
pathloss_at_reference_distances_db.source: The three anchored (a,b,c) triples in this file evaluated at d = 100 m and d = 500 m with fc = 5.9 GHz, in double precision, on 2026-08-30. These are the expected values for the ROADMAP Phase-2 benchmark gate 'implemented 37.885 formulas match published constants to 0.01 dB at d=100/500 m'; frequency terms are 18.2*log10(5.9) = 14.029507, 18.9*log10(5.9) = 14.569103, 20*log10(5.9) = 15.417040 dB.
pathloss_at_reference_distances_db.derivation: PL = a + b*log10(d) + c*log10(5.9), values rounded to 4 decimal places (2.5x tighter than the 0.01 dB gate tolerance, so rounding cannot mask a failure).
pathloss_at_reference_distances_db.note: PINNED FOR PHASE 2 unit tests. Asserting the implementation against these pinned numbers -- rather than against a second copy of the formula -- is what makes the conformance test non-tautological.

value.distribution: extra_loss = max(0, N(mu, sigma)) added to the LOS path loss

nlosv_extra_loss_db.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 NLOSv state: PL = PL_LOS + max(0, N(mu, sigma)) where mu = 9.0 + max(0, 15*log10(d_3D) - 41) with sigma = 4.5 dB when BOTH antennas are below the blocker's height; mu = 5.0 + max(0, 15*log10(d_3D) - 41) with sigma = 4.0 dB when exactly ONE antenna is below; and no additional loss when both are above. Identical wording in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md lines 39-41 and docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(a); the ROADMAP's shorter 'mu = 5..9 + ...' phrasing is the same rule with the branch condition elided.
nlosv_extra_loss_db.note: The mu base selects on blocker height class, NOT on distance; the distance term is shared by both branches. Truncation at 0 makes this a censored Gaussian, so the MEAN extra loss is strictly greater than mu whenever mu is within ~2 sigma of 0 -- draw the Gaussian and clamp, do not shortcut to the mean.

nlosv_blocker_height_m.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 vehicle-blockage modelling: blocker heights 1.6 m for cars and 3.0 m for trucks, drawn per the scenario's truck proportion. Recorded identically in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md line 40 and docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(a).
nlosv_blocker_height_m.note: These heights select the NLOSv branch. AT THE CORRECTED 1.6 m ANTENNA HEIGHT (TR Type 2): a car or motorcycle blocker (1.6 m body) is the EQUALITY case, which the standard puts in Case 3 (mu base 5.0 dB), and a truck or bus (3.0 m) puts both antennas below the blocker, Case 2 (mu base 9.0 dB). SUPERSEDED READING, kept because it was true of this engine until 2026-09-07: at the former 1.5 m antenna height BOTH blocker heights were above both antennas, so every V2V link resolved to the same branch and blocker TYPE had exactly zero effect on the loss. See nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.

nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.status: CORRECTED IN THE ENGINE 2026-09-07. This entry is kept as the record of a defect that existed, not of one that exists. V2X_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M is now 1.6 m.

value.v2v_branch_reached_by_our_model: one_below (TR Case 3, mu 5.0 dB) for a car or motorcycle blocker, both_below (TR Case 2, mu 9.0 dB) for a truck or bus
value.spec_branch_at_its_own_type2_height: one_below (mu 5.0 dB) for a car blocker, both_below for a truck blocker
value.consequence_elsewhere_in_the_model: the two-ray breakpoint d_b = 4*h_TX*h_RX/lambda is quadratic in this height, so it moves from 177.1 m to 201.5 m (+13.8%). Nothing else in the engine reads an antenna height: `disc` and `logdistance` never touch StationSnapshot.ant_h_m, which is why neither pinned dataset digest moves.

nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 6.1.2 vehicle types vs run.py V2X_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M
nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.source: TR 37.885 V15.3.0 CLAUSE 6.1.2 'UE drop and mobility modeling' defines exactly three vehicle types and gives each an ANTENNA height distinct from its BODY height: 'Type 1 (passenger vehicle with lower antenna position): length 5 meters, width 2.0 meters, height 1.6 meters, antenna height 0.75 meters'; 'Type 2 (passenger vehicle with higher antenna position): length 5 meters, width 2.0 meters, height 1.6 meters, antenna height 1.6 meters'; 'Type 3 (truck/bus): length 13 meters, width 2.6 meters, height 3 meters, antenna height 3 meters'. Read first-hand on 2026-09-07 from 37885-f30.docx retrieved from the 3GPP specification archive. This project instead assigns EVERY non-RSU station a single V2X_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M = 1.5 m (run.py) while taking the blocker height from the type table, so antenna height is type-independent and blocker height is type-dependent.
nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.derivation: 1.5 m is below both 1.6 m and 3.0 m, so (tx_h < blk) + (rx_h < blk) == 2 for every V2V pair and every blocker: branch 'both_below', mu 9.0, realised mean E[max(0,N(9.0,4.5))] = 9.038208 dB. Evaluating the same spec rule at the spec's own type-2 antenna height (1.6 m) against a 1.6 m car body gives Case 3, mu 5.0, realised mean 5.202347 dB. Difference 9.038208 - 5.202347 = 3.835861 dB. Recomputed 2026-09-07 against the constants imported live from run.py.
nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.corrected: 2026-09-07 (RADIO-VS-REALITY.md revision 2, W7). THE CLAUSE NUMBER WAS WRONG: this entry and the document said 'clause 5'. The vehicle types are in clause 6.1.2, 'UE drop and mobility modeling'. The quoted text itself was verbatim-exact and is unchanged. ALSO ADDED: 1.5 m is not simply absent from the standard -- it is Table 6.1.4-1's antenna height for a PEDESTRIAN OR CELLULAR UE, against 'Vehicle UE: As defined in Subclause 6.1.2'. The same table gives 'UE-type-RSU: 5 m', which run.py's RSU_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M = 5.0 takes correctly. We took the RSU row right and gave our vehicles the pedestrian row.
nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.corrected_2: 2026-09-07, SECOND PASS: THE DEFECT IS FIXED AND THE STATED BLOCKER WAS IMAGINARY. The note below said the fix was withheld because 'changing V2X_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M moves both pinned dataset digests'. IT DOES NOT, AND THAT WAS TESTED RATHER THAN ARGUED: with the constant at 1.6 m, the reference arm still hashes to b25f2137cf14dd504d56bb88cd67cce273b6a6ac348f7c59ee6d3b4372257815 and the default golden still hashes to 0bd93655a2d5bebb4172191fab0940a5ff90c6be685cfa033f5edcfd7c1fb740. Both pinned arms run radio_model='disc', which never reads StationSnapshot.ant_h_m; only the opt-in geometric model does. The 3.836 dB defect was therefore fixable at zero pinned-digest cost for as long as the entry claimed otherwise. FIXED TOGETHER WITH nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence, and the two could not be separated: at 1.6 m antennas against 1.6 m car bodies the equality case becomes the commonest urban NLOSv geometry there is, so correcting the height alone would have swapped a +3.836 dB error for a -5.2023 dB one.
nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance.note: WAS OUR DEFECT, NOT THE STANDARD'S; NOW CORRECTED. The 1.5 m choice inflated car/motorcycle blockage by 3.836 dB relative to the standard we claim to implement, and it collapsed the standard's three-case rule to a single case for all V2V traffic -- blocker TYPE could not affect a V2V link at all. Kept as a record because the ERROR is instructive: 1.5 m is not absent from TR 37.885, it is the PEDESTRIAN UE row of the very table the RSU height (5 m) was read correctly from. CAUTION ON MOTIVATION, UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDING: revision 1 of RADIO-VS-REALITY.md justified this fix by claiming it would restore 'near-exact agreement with measurement'. That claim is WITHDRAWN -- the 5 dB it pointed at is GEMV^2 model output, not a measurement (see nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output). The fix was made as CONFORMANCE; it buys no demonstrated agreement with reality, and the NLOSv term remains falsified against measurement in the way nlosv_loss_is_flat_with_distance_but_measurement_decays records. See docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md sections 0 and 4.

nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.status: CORRECTED IN THE ENGINE 2026-09-07. run.py's `tr37885_nlosv_case` now implements the standard's three cases as written, and it is the only place the branch is decided.

value.divergent_input: min(antenna height) exactly equal to blocker height

nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 6.2.1 three-case rule vs run.py _link_state
nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.source: TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 6.2.1, quoted verbatim: 'The additional blockage loss is max {0 dB, a log-normal random variable}'; 'Case 1: Minimum antenna height value of TX and RX > Blocker height - No additional blockage loss'; 'Case 2: Maximum antenna height value of TX and RX < Blocker height - Mean: 9 + max(0, 15*log10(d)-41) dB, standard deviation: 4.5 dB'; 'Case 3: Otherwise - Mean: 5 dB + max(0, 15*log10(d)-41), standard deviation: 4 dB'. run.py computes the branch as below = (tx_h < blocker_h) + (rx_h < blocker_h) and maps below==0 to the zero-loss case. below==0 means min(h) >= blocker_h, but the standard's Case 1 requires min(h) STRICTLY greater; the equality input belongs to Case 3.
nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.derivation: Enumerating all 27 ordered (tx type, rx type, blocker type) triples over the TR's own three vehicle types, our rule and the standard's rule disagree on 7, always in the same direction: we return 0.0 dB where the standard returns mu 5.0 dB (realised 5.202347 dB). The bias then depends on WHICH of the TR's own UE-dropping options is used to weight the triples; all are enumerated in bias_by_tr37885_dropping_option below. Computed 2026-09-07 against the live constants imported from run.py.
nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.corrected: 2026-09-07 (RADIO-VS-REALITY.md revision 2, W6). THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY REPORTED A SINGLE bias_under_tr37885_urban_fleet_mix_db OF -2.539 AND ATTRIBUTED IT TO 'the TR's own urban type distribution (20/60/20)', AS IF THERE WERE ONLY ONE. TR 37.885 clause 6.1.2 defines TWO urban-grid UE-dropping options, quoted verbatim: 'Option A - Vehicle type distribution: 100% vehicle type 2.' and 'Option B - Vehicle type distribution: 20% vehicle type 1, 60% vehicle type 2, 20% vehicles type 3.' The definite article concealed a choice, and the chosen option was the flattering one: under Option A the bias is -5.2023 dB, exactly DOUBLE the reported figure, because every type-2 antenna (1.6 m) equals every car body (1.6 m) and so EVERY urban NLOSv link is the equality case. The highway scenario adds a third option, 'Option C - Vehicle type distribution: 0% vehicle type 1, 67% vehicle type 2, 33% vehicle type 3', giving -3.2930 dB. All five enumerated above against the live constants. No model input changed.
nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.corrected_2: 2026-09-07, SECOND PASS: FIXED, AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE AS nlosv_antenna_height_nonconformance BECAUSE NEITHER COULD BE FIXED ALONE. The note below correctly predicted the trap -- 'fixing the antenna heights without also fixing this comparison would swap a +3.84 dB error for a -5.20 dB one' -- and that is exactly what would have happened: at 1.6 m antennas against 1.6 m car bodies the equality case is not a corner, it is the commonest urban NLOSv geometry in the project. run.py's branch test is now `tr37885_nlosv_case`, a single function implementing the standard's three cases verbatim, and it agrees with an independent transcription on every one of the 27 type triples and on every height triple the project can produce. The note's last sentence, 'both pinned digests forbid changing either today', was FALSE and was disproved by re-running both arms: neither moves, because both run radio_model='disc'.
nlosv_branch_boundary_divergence.note: WAS LATENT, NOW MOOT. The equality case was unreachable while vehicles sat at 1.5 m and RSUs at 5.0 m, so the divergence cost nothing in practice -- but it was one antenna-height correction away from becoming the dominant case, which is what makes it worth having recorded. Kept as the record of a fix whose ORDER mattered more than its content.

value.spec_rule: P(LOS) = min{1, 1.05*exp(-0.0114*d)} for the urban case; P(NLOSv) = 1 - P(LOS)
value.our_rule: deterministic ray test against the vehicle blocker index (GEO_BLOCKER_HALF_WIDTH_M corridor), then the three-case height rule
value.measured_on: the reference arm (--flow --road grid --grid 6 --duration 300 --arrival-rate 2 --attacker-pct 0.15 --traffic-lights --seed 42) re-run under radio_model='geometric' with radio_nlosb_density_per_km=0 so no NLOSb can absorb the difference; 4,261,310 classified link-steps, 2026-09-07
value.sign_of_the_deviation: NOT ONE-SIDED. Below ~60 m we classify MORE links NLOSv than the standard's probability does (2.5x at 0-25 m, where the standard says a 12 m link is 91% LOS and our own vehicles are 5 m long); above ~100 m we classify far FEWER (3.5-4.4x). The crossover sits at about 60 m.

los_nlosv_classification_is_geometric_no.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 Table 6.2-1 vs run.py GeometricChannel._link_state
los_nlosv_classification_is_geometric_no.source: TR 37.885 V15.3.0 Table 6.2-1 gives the LOS probability as a FUNCTION OF DISTANCE ONLY, per scenario -- urban 'min(1, 1.05*exp(-0.0114*d))', with NLOSv taking the remainder -- and clause 6.2.1 then draws the blocker's height statistically ('The blocker height is the vehicle height which is randomly selected out of the three vehicle types according to the portion of the vehicle types in the simulated scenario'). This project instead resolves both GEOMETRICALLY: `_VehicleBlockerIndex.tallest_blocker_entry` ray-tests the actual vehicles between the two endpoints and takes the tallest, and the case rule then uses that blocker's real height. Measured against the standard's own curve on the reference arm's traffic (see measured_on).
los_nlosv_classification_is_geometric_no.note: A DELIBERATE, NAMED DEVIATION -- recorded because it was recorded NOWHERE before, not because it is a defect. The geometric rule is arguably the better instrument: it responds to density, to lane geometry and to a queue at a red light, none of which a distance-only probability can express, and this project's whole reason for classifying per link is that a misbehaviour detector reads the resulting burst structure. What is NOT defensible is claiming conformance to TR 37.885's channel while diverging from its Table 6.2-1 by a factor of 3.53 overall and in BOTH DIRECTIONS across the band. The honest statement is: we implement the standard's path loss, its shadowing, its blockage distribution and its three-case rule, and we substitute our own LOS/NLOSv classifier for its probability model. Anyone reproducing a TR 37.885 evaluation-methodology result must know that.

value.closed_by: radio_antenna_pattern='tr37885_opt1', which adds the element gain at both ends

link_budget_is_6db_below_tr37885_by_defa.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 Table 6.1.1-1 and Table 6.1.4-8 vs run.py radio_tx_power_dbm
link_budget_is_6db_below_tr37885_by_defa.source: TR 37.885 Table 6.1.1-1 lists transmit powers in one column: 'BS Tx power -- Macro BS: 49dBm ... Micro BS: 24dBm' and 'UE Tx power -- Vehicle/pedestrian UE or UE type RSU: 23dBm'. 49 dBm is a macro base station's CONDUCTED PA power, and the antenna element gain is given SEPARATELY in Table 6.1.4-8 ('Max direct. gain of the antenna element -- 3 dBi'). The only occurrence of 'e.i.r.p.' in the document is in clause 5, a 63-64 GHz regulatory survey, not in the simulation assumptions. So the TR-conformant V2V budget is 23 dBm conducted + 3 dBi transmit element gain - PL + 3 dBi receive element gain.
link_budget_is_6db_below_tr37885_by_defa.note: THIS INVERTS AN EARLIER RECOMMENDATION, and the earlier one is named so the reversal is auditable. docs/realism/CHANNEL-PHYSICS.md revision 1 held radio_antenna_pattern OFF pending an 'EIRP double count', on the grounds that run.py documented radio_tx_power_dbm as EIRP and an EIRP already contains the transmit gain. The comment was the bug, not the arithmetic: read as the standard writes it, the pattern-ON budget is the conformant one and the shipped default is 6 dB LOW. THE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN RESOLVED: run.py's own justification for 23 dBm is an ETSI EIRP argument ('ETSI caps EIRP at 33'), so this repository does hold two conventions for one number. Under the ETSI reading the value would be an EIRP and the transmit element gain would be a double count; under the TR reading it is conducted and the pattern closes a gap. The number 23 is defensible either way, which is exactly why the ambiguity survived unnoticed. The diagnostic arm that sets the transmit power to a conducted 20 dBm (tools/channel_physics.py) is the NON-conformant one against TR 37.885 and is labelled so.

rsu_antenna_arrays_are_not_modelled.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 Tables 6.1.4-1 to 6.1.4-5 vs run.py GeometricChannel._station_antenna
rsu_antenna_arrays_are_not_modelled.source: TR 37.885 models an RSU with a BS-type or UE-type antenna ARRAY -- panel counts, bearings, downtilt and a TXRU mapping (Tables 6.1.4-1 to 6.1.4-5) -- and this channel has no array factor to evaluate one through. The vehicle arm implements only the single-ELEMENT pattern of Table 6.1.4-8. A VRU is different and is NOT a gap: Table 6.1.4-6 gives a pedestrian UE an omnidirectional element with 0 dBi max gain, which is exactly what the model applies.
rsu_antenna_arrays_are_not_modelled.note: REFUSED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED, 2026-09-07. Returning 0 dB for an RSU endpoint -- which is what the first version of the antenna term did, counting the omission in `stats` -- gives every V2V link 2 x 3 dBi and every V2I link 3 dBi, i.e. a PERMANENT 3 dB relative penalty on infrastructure links that comes from a missing model rather than from physics, and that would be invisible in any aggregate. The antenna term was recommended having been measured on ZERO RSU links ('No scene here has RSUs'), and n_rsus defaults to 0, so the defect was latent -- but --rsus is a shipped knob and the MA report path uses RSUs. validate_config now rejects radio_antenna_pattern != 'none' together with n_rsus > 0, and the channel raises if it is reached with validation bypassed. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an array-factor implementation for Tables 6.1.4-1..-5, at which point the refusal becomes a modelled gain and V2I links can be compared with V2V ones again.

nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output.cite: Boban, Barros & Tonguz, IEEE TVT 63(9):4146-4164, 2014 (preprint arXiv:1305.0124v3), Fig. 12
nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output.source: PROVENANCE RECORD, NOT DATA. The widely-quoted '5, 13 and 20 dB for car, van and truck at 100 m' triple is GEMV^2 SIMULATOR OUTPUT, not a measurement. Figure 12's own caption, verbatim: 'Received power distribution AS GENERATED BY GEMV^2 for LOS links and NLOSv links due to three vehicle types: passenger car (mean height: 1.5 meters), commercial van (mean height: 2 meters), and truck (mean height: 3 meters); standard deviation for the height of each vehicle type was set to 0.15 meters. For each link, a single vehicle of a given type is placed between transmitter and receiver, both of which are passenger cars with the height of 1.5 meters. Distance between transmitter and receiver is uniformly distributed between 75 and 125 meters. Transmit power is set to 10 dBm and gains at both transmit and receive antenna are 1 dBi.' The body text adds that these results are 'IN LINE WITH previous measurements reported in [3], [6], [36]' -- consistent with, not drawn from, measurement. The numbers themselves are IEEE copyright and are NOT committed here; they are quoted with attribution in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 1.
nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output.consumer_retracted: 2026-09-07, SAME DAY: THE ARM THIS ENTRY WARNED ABOUT IS GONE. radio_nlosv_model and every BOBAN_* constant were removed from run.py, and the knob with them, so nothing in the tree now anchors on this triple. Four reasons, any one sufficient: (a) the level anchor is the GEMV^2 output described below, so the arm was not measurement-based; (b) graded against Segata et al. (IEEE VNC 2013, the one independent 5.9 GHz truck-blockage measurement in its own citation set) the arm's error was +11 to +15 dB where the SPECIFICATION it replaced was -0.96 / +4.04 dB, i.e. one-sided and an order of magnitude worse; (c) no measurement in its chain was a car blocking a car link, and its '5-7 dB at 100 m' pair mixed an 802.11p van with an 802.11b/g van at 2412 MHz; (d) LICENCE -- digitising an IEEE-copyright figure into a source constant is exactly what this project's standing rule forbids. THE FILE-VS-FILE CONTRADICTION THIS ENTRY RECORDED IS THEREFORE RESOLVED: the tree no longer asserts two opposite things about the same triple. The retraction is written up as a negative result in the section-2 block comment of run.py, in tests/test_geometric_channel_physics.py (which pins the constants as absent), and in docs/realism/CHANNEL-PHYSICS.md section 6 R2.
nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output.consumers_that_must_carry_this_label: HISTORIC, AND THE SUBJECT OF consumer_retracted ABOVE. AS OF 2026-09-07 THE OPT-IN ARM radio_nlosv_model='measured_boban' IN run.py ANCHORS ITS 100 m LEVEL ON THIS TRIPLE -- BOBAN_NLOSV_MU_AT_100M_DB = {'car': 5.0, 'truck': 20.0} -- WHILE CALLING ITSELF A 'MEASUREMENT-BASED ARM'. Its SLOPE anchor (20 dB at 10 m falling to 7 dB at 100 m) IS a measurement, from arXiv:1405.1008 section 2.3.1; its LEVEL anchor is this GEMV^2 output. nlosv_blockage_draw_is_per_packet_not_pe.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 6.2.1 vs run.py evaluate_raw
nlosv_blockage_draw_is_per_packet_not_pe.source: TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 6.2.1, verbatim: 'The additional blockage loss is max {0 dB, a log-normal random variable}.' A log-normal random variable attached to a blocked LINK is a large-scale effect of the same class as shadow fading -- one realisation held while the link stays blocked. run.py instead draws it inside evaluate_raw, which runs once per packet, so a link parked behind the same truck receives an independent sigma = 4.5 dB draw on EVERY CAM. Note that the Gudmundson AR(1) shadowing sitting immediately above it in the same function IS correctly carried per link across steps (state dict key 's'); only the blockage term is not.
nlosv_blockage_draw_is_per_packet_not_pe.derivation: Three consequences, all in the direction that flatters our own gates: (1) a large-scale term is converted into fast fading, a category error; (2) burst-loss runs are SHORTENED, because a link that should sit reliably ~15 dB down for a second instead flickers, which flatters the packet-inter-reception tail and the awareness ratio the Phase-2 gate reads; (3) it DOUBLE-COUNTS against the per-packet Nakagami fade drawn on the next line, so a blocked link carries two independent per-packet random terms where the standard specifies one per-packet and one per-link.
nlosv_blockage_draw_is_per_packet_not_pe.corrected_2: 2026-09-07, SECOND PASS: 'ONE DRAW PER BLOCKED LINK' IS NOT IN THE STANDARD, AND THIS ENTRY SAID IT WAS. Clause 6.2.1 read in full gives the blockage loss as 'max {0 dB, a log-normal random variable}' and states NO temporal scope for the draw -- not per link, not per packet. The stronger reading was asserted in the task brief that commissioned the opt-in arm and was inherited into run.py, into tests/test_geometric_channel_physics.py, into docs/realism/CHANNEL-PHYSICS.md and into this entry, all of which labelled the arm CONFORMANT. That label is WITHDRAWN in all four places. Two further reasons it was wrong rather than merely unsupported: (a) the standard's blocker is STATISTICAL, not geometric -- 'The blocker height is the vehicle height which is randomly selected out of the three vehicle types according to the portion of the vehicle types in the simulated scenario' -- whereas the implementation keys its held deviate to a geometrically identified vehicle the standard does not have; (b) where the standard IS explicit about persistence it is STRONGER than the implementation: 'Baseline is the state is not updated between LOS and NLOSv', i.e. held for the whole link lifetime, which the arm's own 'a different vehicle means a new episode' rule breaks. THE TERM STAYS, on physics: a blockage is a large-scale effect, drawing it per packet demotes it to fast fading and double-counts against the per-packet Nakagami fade, and the measured effect is real (see measured_effect_of_the_hold). What is withdrawn is the claim that a standard requires it.
nlosv_blockage_draw_is_per_packet_not_pe.note: OUR DEFECT, NOT THE STANDARD'S -- but 'defect' here means a MODELLING one (a large-scale term drawn as fast fading), not a conformance one, and the distinction is the whole of corrected_2. Ranked gap G1 in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 7. STILL THE DEFAULT: the opt-in arm (radio_nlosv_hold) defaults to False, so the per-packet draw is what every pinned digest and every gate still measures. Its effect on the awareness gate has NOT been quantified; doing so requires an A/B that moves the digests.

no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 6.1.4 (Antenna model) vs run.py GeometricChannel
no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term.source: IN THE DEFAULT CONFIGURATION run.py's entire link budget is one line: `mean_rx = self.tx_dbm - pl + shadow_db`, with no gain, no pattern and no bearing -- both endpoints radiate isotropically at every angle, and received power is provably independent of link bearing (pinned in tests/test_geometric_channel.py). TR 37.885 clause 6.1.4 specifies the opposite, per vehicle type, in two alternative options. OPTION 1 (Tables 6.1.4-8 and 6.1.4-9): the element's horizontal gain pattern is given separately for 'Vehicle Type 2' and for 'Vehicle Type 1 and Type 3', and the array configuration puts types 1 and 3 on front and rear antennas with 'Front antenna array bearing angle: Omega_Front = 0 deg' and 'Rear antenna array bearing angle: Omega_Rear = 180 deg', while type 2 gets a rooftop antenna; max element gain 3 dBi at 6 GHz. OPTION 2 (Tables 6.1.4-10A to 10D and 6.1.4-12): 'For vehicle type 1, one panel at the front bumper and one panel at the rear bumper'; 'For vehicle type 2, one panel at the front rooftop and one panel at the rear rooftop'; likewise type 3. Max element gain 13 dBi front bumper, 11 dBi rear bumper, 3 dBi rooftop. The standard notes 'that self-blockage effect is captured Option 2 in the antenna pattern'. Read first-hand from 37885-f30.docx on 2026-09-07.
no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term.corrected: 2026-09-07, SECOND PASS: THE 'UNLOCKS NILSSON' CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN. The note below, and the matching comment in run.py, said that switching the opt-in arm on makes Nilsson et al.'s 2-4 m de-correlation distance 'an APPLICABLE comparison for the first time'. It does not, on the source's own terms. Their 2.2/3.7 m medians are measured on the ZERO-MEAN, offset-subtracted large-scale process, and they say where the offset goes: 'The mean of Psi-sigma ... represents the differences in the particular traffic situation and THE GAIN OF THE INVOLVED ANTENNAS for the particular communication link.' Their conditional asks for a model of the PER-LINK antenna gain; this arm supplies a STATISTICAL ELEMENT pattern from a specification, and for the Type 2 pair that is ~70% of these fleets it is a CONSTANT +3 dBi at every bearing, removing no per-link variation at all. Turning it on does not move a model of this class out of the source's 'otherwise' branch, and intersection_measured_decorrelation_distance_m in this same file already said so. TR37885_SHADOW_DECORR_M is unchanged and is not re-litigated.
no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term.note: THE LARGEST SINGLE OMISSION IN THE CHANNEL MODEL (gap G2), AND IT IS ALSO A CONFOUND, NOT ONLY A GAP. Because the default has no antenna-pattern term, this model sits in the 'otherwise' branch of Nilsson et al.'s conditional -- 'In cases where a proper model for the path loss AND THE ANTENNA PATTERN is included, the de-correlation distance ... is as low as 2-4 m ... OTHERWISE, the de-correlation distance has to be much longer' -- which is why the earlier 'decorrelation is falsified' finding had to be withdrawn (see intersection_measured_decorrelation_distance_m). STATUS 2026-09-07: an opt-in Option-1 arm (radio_antenna_pattern='tr37885_opt1', radio_antenna_gain_dbi) exists and defaults to 'none', so the omission is still what every pinned digest and every gate measures. WHAT THE ARM ACTUALLY BUYS, now that the EIRP question is settled: it closes a 6 dB LINK-BUDGET conformance gap, not a de-correlation one -- see link_budget_is_6db_below_tr37885_by_default. WHAT IT REFUSES: RSU endpoints, see rsu_antenna_arrays_are_not_modelled. See docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 7 G2.

value.our_model: single slope at all distances: PL = a + b*log10(d) + c*log10(fc), b = 16.7 dB/decade for urban LOS

no_two_ray_breakpoint_in_pathloss.cite: Abbas et al., IJAP 2015 Art. 190607 (CC BY 3.0), Table II and the breakpoint derivation, vs run.py TR37885_PATHLOSS
no_two_ray_breakpoint_in_pathloss.source: run.py's TR37885_PATHLOSS is single-slope for every state and every distance. Abbas et al. fit a DUAL-slope model with a physical breakpoint, verbatim: 'For the measurement setup the height of the TX/RX antennas was hTX = hRX = 1.47 m, thus, db can be calculated as, db = (4*hTX*hRX - lambda^2/4)/lambda = 161 m for lambda = 0.0536 m at 5.6 GHz carrier frequency. A db of 104 m was selected to match the values with the path loss model presented in [20], implying a somewhat better fit to the measurement data.' Their Table II gives the far-field channel-gain exponents n2 = -2.85 (urban LOS), -2.74 (urban OLOS), -2.88 (highway LOS), i.e. path-loss slopes of 28.5, 27.4 and 28.8 dB/decade.
no_two_ray_breakpoint_in_pathloss.derivation: At OUR OWN geometry -- 1.6 m antennas (TR 37.885 Type 2), fc 5.9 GHz, lambda = 0.050812 m -- the same expression gives db = 201.5 m, INSIDE the operating range of every scenario in this project. Our urban LOS decays at 16.7 dB/decade everywhere, so beyond the breakpoint we are missing 28.5 - 16.7 = 11.8 dB/decade. SUPERSEDED FIGURES, computed 2026-09-07 at the then-current 1.5 m antenna height and kept for continuity: db = 177.1 m gave an under-prediction of 0.62 dB at 200 m / 2.70 dB at 300 m / 5.32 dB at 500 m; with Abbas's fitted db = 104 m, 3.35 dB / 5.43 dB / 8.05 dB. The breakpoint is QUADRATIC in antenna height, so correcting 1.5 -> 1.6 m moved it out by 13.8% and every figure in this entry that depends on db moves with it; the direction and the missing 11.8 dB/decade do not.
no_two_ray_breakpoint_in_pathloss.note: THE ABSENCE OF ANY BREAKPOINT TERM IS CONFIRMED. THE MAGNITUDE ABOVE IS PLAUSIBLE, NOT CONFIRMED -- it spans a factor of five across two legitimate breakpoint choices, and TR 37.885's urban fit may legitimately embed street-canyon waveguiding that a flat-earth two-ray model does not represent, which is exactly the kind of environment Abbas's urban rows also contain. The confidence field is 'coarse' for that reason. WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT IS THE SIGN: we under-predict path loss beyond ~180 m, which inflates long-range awareness AND long-range interference together. STATUS 2026-09-07: an opt-in arm (radio_breakpoint='two_ray', radio_breakpoint_slope_db_per_decade) landed from a concurrent workstream and defaults to 'none', so single-slope is still what every pinned digest measures. Gap G3 in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 7.

nlosv_loss_is_flat_with_distance_but_mea.cite: derived from run.py; the measured counter-evidence is quoted (not committed) in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 5
nlosv_loss_is_flat_with_distance_but_mea.source: STRUCTURAL FACT ABOUT OUR MODEL, computed from the live constants: because the TR 37.885 distance term max(0, 15*log10(d) - 41) is identically zero below 10^(41/15) = 541.1695 m, the realised NLOSv mean takes exactly ONE value, 9.038208 dB, over 1-541 m, and then INCREASES. Two MEASURED campaigns report the opposite behaviour over the band our scenarios occupy, both stating it in BODY TEXT rather than in a figure: Boban's PhD thesis section 2.3.1 (arXiv:1405.1008) for a van blocker at 802.11p / 5900 MHz with the blocker 37 cm above the antenna tips -- our both_below branch exactly, standard deviation under 1 dB -- and Segata et al. (IEEE VNC 2013 section IV) for a truck blocker at 5.89 GHz. BOTH SOURCES ARE NON-CC (arXiv non-exclusive licence and IEEE copyright respectively), so THEIR NUMBERS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED HERE; they are quoted with attribution in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 5, which is the licence-compliant place for them.
nlosv_loss_is_flat_with_distance_but_mea.note: FALSIFIED, AND THE ERROR CHANGES SIGN. Our excess loss is too small at short range and too large at medium range, so no single additive correction fixes both ends, and the measurement's own scatter (std dev under 1 dB, 'confidence intervals too small to represent') cannot absorb it. This is TR 37.885's limitation, transcribed faithfully -- not a transcription error of ours -- and it bounds what 'realistic radio' can mean for this project until a distance-dependent NLOSv term exists. SUPERSEDES an earlier record that called this 'unresolved -- could not verify': both sources are openly reachable and text-extractable, and that entry was a retrieval failure, not a gap in the literature. STATUS 2026-09-07, END OF DAY: an opt-in arm (radio_nlosv_model='measured_boban') landed and was RETRACTED the same day; see nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output.consumer_retracted. Graded against Segata et al. the replacement was one-sidedly +11 to +15 dB wrong where the specification is -0.96 / +4.04 dB, so THE SPECIFIED TERM SURVIVES ITS OWN FALSIFICATION AS THE BEST AVAILABLE OPTION -- which is the useful result here, and the reason this entry is not softened: the flat term is still wrong in the way described below, and there is now no arm that is less wrong. See docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md sections 5 and 7.7, and ROADMAP-PERFECT.md P7c.

blockage_spread_and_footprint_ignore_blo.cite: run.py TR37885_NLOSV + GEO_BLOCKER_HALF_WIDTH_M vs TR 37.885 clause 6.1.2; measured counter-evidence in Segata et al., IEEE VNC 2013
blockage_spread_and_footprint_ignore_blo.source: Verified against the live constants on 2026-09-07: every entry of TR37885_BLOCKER_HEIGHT_M is taller than V2X_ANTENNA_HEIGHT_M, so all four blocker types resolve to the 'both_below' branch and carry sigma = 4.5 dB identically -- a motorcycle and an articulated truck have the same blockage SPREAD as well as the same MEAN. Separately, run.py's GEO_BLOCKER_HALF_WIDTH_M = 1.0 is a single constant applied to every vehicle, while TR 37.885 clause 6.1.2 gives 'length 5 meters, width 2.0 meters' for types 1 and 2 and 'length 13 meters, width 2.6 meters' for type 3, so blocker type affects neither WHETHER a link is blocked, nor HOW MUCH it loses, nor WITH WHAT SPREAD. Segata et al. (IEEE VNC 2013, section IV) measure the spread directly and report that the bigger the obstacle the higher the variance, and that different distribution parameters should therefore be used per blocker type; their exact wording is IEEE copyright and is quoted with attribution in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 7 G4 rather than committed here.
blockage_spread_and_footprint_ignore_blo.corrected: 2026-09-07, SECOND PASS. HALF OF G4 CLOSED AS A SIDE EFFECT OF THE ANTENNA-HEIGHT FIX, and it is worth being precise about which half. With antennas at the standard's own 1.6 m the three-case rule no longer collapses: a car or motorcycle is TR Case 3 (sigma 4.0 dB) and a truck or bus is TR Case 2 (sigma 4.5 dB), so a bigger blocker now does carry a bigger spread -- the DIRECTION Segata et al. report -- and it does so because the STANDARD says so, not because anything was fitted. What is NOT closed: the split is two-valued and comes from the antenna-vs-body geometry, not from blocker size as such, so a motorcycle and a saloon car remain identical and the gap between 4.0 and 4.5 dB is not claimed to be the measured one.
blockage_spread_and_footprint_ignore_blo.note: GAPS G4 (PARTLY CLOSED) AND G5. The earlier record cited Segata et al. only for the MEAN; their result is about the DISTRIBUTION, which is what their title claims and what these two gaps are. STATUS 2026-09-07: G5 has an opt-in arm (radio_blocker_width='tr37885', default 'uniform'). G4 IS STILL NOT CLOSED AS STATED, AND CANNOT BE YET: no licence-clean source found states a fitted blockage sigma per blocker CLASS -- Nilsson et al.'s Table 3 splits on the TRANSMITTER's type, not the blocker's, and its two intersections disagree in sign -- so a genuinely blocker-size-dependent sigma is blocked on evidence, not on effort, and inventing a split would be fabrication. THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS ENTRY RECORDS: what would settle it is a per-blocker-class sigma stated in the text or a table of a redistributable source. See docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 7.

value.our_rule: Nakagami-m power drawn i.i.d. per packet (run.py: prng.gammavariate(m, 1.0/m))

small_scale_fade_has_no_temporal_correla.cite: derived: Clarke/Jakes coherence time 0.423/f_D at fc = 5.9 GHz vs the ETSI CAM period
small_scale_fade_has_no_temporal_correla.source: run.py draws the small-scale fade independently for every packet, with no state carried between them. Coherence time is taken here as Tc = 0.423/f_D with f_D = v_rel/lambda and lambda = c/5.9e9 = 0.050812 m; computed at double precision on 2026-09-07. At 30 m/s relative speed f_D = 590.4 Hz and Tc = 0.72 ms, three orders of magnitude below the 100 ms CAM period, so i.i.d. per packet is defensible. At 0.1 m/s -- two vehicles stopped at the same signal, with near-zero RELATIVE speed -- f_D = 1.97 Hz and Tc = 215 ms, longer than two CAM periods.
small_scale_fade_has_no_temporal_correla.note: GAP G6, AND IT BITES EXACTLY ON THE REFERENCE ARM. The pinned reference run uses --traffic-lights, which forms queues, which is precisely where relative speed goes to zero and where i.i.d. per-packet fading is optimistic: real links stay inside the same fade across several consecutive CAMs, so real burst losses are longer than ours. Confidence is 'coarse' because 0.423/f_D is one of several conventions for coherence time (the 9/(16*pi*f_D) form gives ~0.42x these values) and because nothing here has been compared against a measurement -- the CONCLUSION (i.i.d. is optimistic at a stop line) is robust to the convention; the specific milliseconds are not. Lowest rank of the six gaps only because a fix needs a correlated fading process and its own validation. See docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 7 G6.

nlosv_has_no_measurement_provenance_in_t.cite: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 clause 2 (References) and Annex B (Change history)
nlosv_has_no_measurement_provenance_in_t.source: The complete reference list of TR 37.885 V15.3.0 was read first-hand on 2026-09-07 from the ATIS mirror. It contains nineteen entries: [1]-[5] and [13]-[18] are 3GPP TRs and work-item proposals (21.905, RP-170837, 22.886, 38.913, 38.802, 36.885, 36.873, 38.901, 36.872, 36.814, 22.872); [6]-[11] are ITU-R, ECC, ETSI and IEEE 802.18 spectrum and regulatory documents about the 63-64 GHz band; [12] is the Republic of Korea table of frequency allocations; and [19] is F. Gil et al., 'A 3-D extrapolation model for base station antenna's radiation patterns', Proc. IEEE VTC-Fall 1999 -- an antenna-pattern paper, not a propagation campaign. NOT ONE of the nineteen is a V2V propagation measurement campaign. Annex B records the NLOSv term's only provenance as change request RP-182530 CR 0004 category F, 'Correction on vehicle blockage loss in NLOSv', agreed at RAN#82 in 2018-12 for version 15.2.0.
nlosv_has_no_measurement_provenance_in_t.note: STRUCTURAL, AND IT FRAMES EVERY OTHER NLOSv ENTRY IN THIS FILE. The 9.0/5.0 dB means, the 4.5/4.0 dB sigmas and the max(0, 15*log10(d)-41) distance term are treated throughout this project as anchored constants, and they are faithfully transcribed -- but the document they are transcribed FROM cites no measurement for them. 'Anchored' here therefore means 'anchored to a standard', never 'anchored to data'. The empirical checks live in the sibling entries (nlosv_measured_single_vehicle_loss_db, intersection_measured_shadowing_sigma_db, measured_decorrelation_is_environment_dependent) and in docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md, which is where the term is actually confronted with measurements.

nlosv_distance_term_activation_m.cite: derived from the TR 37.885 NLOSv mu expression
nlosv_distance_term_activation_m.source: The NLOSv distance term max(0, 15*log10(d) - 41) is identically zero until 15*log10(d) = 41, i.e. d = 10^(41/15) = 541.1695 m. Computed at double precision on 2026-08-30 from the anchored expression in nlosv_extra_loss_db.
nlosv_distance_term_activation_m.derivation: 10^(41/15) = 541.1695 m; below it mu is exactly 9.0 dB (both below) or 5.0 dB (one below), with no distance dependence at all.
nlosv_distance_term_activation_m.note: IMPLEMENTER NOTE: across the whole urban regime the NLOSv mean extra loss is a CONSTANT. A unit test that only probes d < 541 m cannot distinguish a correct distance term from a missing one -- probe d = 1000 m (mu = 13.0 dB both-below) as well.

nlosv_measured_single_vehicle_loss_db.cite: multi-band V2V blockage measurement campaign (typical ~10 dB, Boban JSAC)
nlosv_measured_single_vehicle_loss_db.source: Measured attenuation caused by a single blocking vehicle is 5.5-17 dB depending on blocker size (multi-band V2V vehicle-blockage characterisation, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330330604), with Boban's earlier IEEE JSAC work reporting ~10 dB as typical for one obstructing vehicle. Summarised in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(f) and restated in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md line 41 as the empirical basis for the 37.885 NLOSv mu of 5-9 dB.
nlosv_measured_single_vehicle_loss_db.note: This is the EMPIRICAL SANITY BAND for the modelled NLOSv draw, not a second model. Check: mu 9.0 dB with sigma 4.5 dB truncated at 0 puts the bulk of draws inside 5.5-17 dB, so a Phase-2 histogram of realised NLOSv losses whose p10-p90 lands far outside this band indicates a coding error, not a modelling choice.

shadowing_sigma_db.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 shadow fading: sigma = 3 dB for LOS and for NLOSv, 4 dB for NLOS. Stated as '3.0 dB (LOS and NLOSv), 4.0 dB (NLOS)' in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(a), as 'sigma 3.0 LOS+NLOSv / 4.0 NLOS' in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md, and adopted in docs/realism/ROADMAP.md section 3.2 item 3 together with a Gudmundson AR(1) correlation process.
shadowing_sigma_db.note: NLOSv keeps the LOS sigma because its extra blockage loss is already modelled as its own random variable (nlosv_extra_loss_db); applying the NLOS 4 dB sigma to an NLOSv link double-counts the blockage spread. Decorrelation distances are in shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.

shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.source: 3GPP TR 37.885 V15.3.0 gives the shadow-fading spatial autocorrelation distance as 10 m for LOS and 13 m for NLOSv and NLOS. Transcribed in docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(a) ('spatial autocorrelation distance 10 m (LOS) / 13 m (NLOSv, NLOS)') and in docs/realism/PHASE2-DESIGN.md ('decorrelation 10 m LOS / 13 m NLOS').
shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m.note: DISAGREEMENT WITH THE SIBLING ENTRY, resolved: v2x_awareness.shadowing_decorrelation_distance_m pins the interval [7, 13] m, which is the ROADMAP's '10 +/- 3 m (ETSI TR 103 257-1)' self-test tolerance -- a GATE on the measured e-folding distance, not a per-state model input. This entry holds the per-state MODEL INPUTS. They are consistent: both TR 37.885 values fall inside [7, 13]. Use this entry to drive the AR(1) process and that entry to grade the resulting autocorrelation.

intersection_measured_shadowing_sigma_db.cite: Nilsson, Gustafson, Abbas & Tufvesson, Sensors 18(12):4433, 2018 (CC BY 4.0)
intersection_measured_shadowing_sigma_db.source: M. G. Nilsson, C. Gustafson, T. Abbas and F. Tufvesson, 'A Path Loss and Shadowing Model for Multilink Vehicle-to-Vehicle Channels in Urban Intersections', Sensors 18(12):4433, 2018, doi:10.3390/s18124433, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6308981/ . 5.9 GHz multilink V2V measurements between six vehicles at two Gothenburg intersections (Yngve, a T-junction; Xerxes, an X-junction). intersection_measured_decorrelation_dist.cite: Nilsson, Gustafson, Abbas & Tufvesson, Sensors 18(12):4433, 2018 (CC BY 4.0)
intersection_measured_decorrelation_dist.source: The same Gothenburg multilink campaign (M. G. Nilsson, C. Gustafson, T. Abbas and F. Tufvesson, 'A Path Loss and Shadowing Model for Multilink Vehicle-to-Vehicle Channels in Urban Intersections', Sensors 18(12):4433, 2018, doi:10.3390/s18124433) measures a MEDIAN shadowing de-correlation distance across all NLOS links of 3.7 m at Yngve and 2.2 m at Xerxes (Figure 12 histograms, medians stated in the text).
intersection_measured_decorrelation_dist.conditional_that_governs_these_numbers: QUOTE THE WHOLE SENTENCE PAIR OR NOT AT ALL. Abstract, verbatim: 'In cases where a proper model for the path loss AND THE ANTENNA PATTERN is included, the de-correlation distance for the auto-correlation is as low as 2-4 m, and the cross-correlation for the large scale fading between different links can be neglected. OTHERWISE, THE DE-CORRELATION DISTANCE HAS TO BE MUCH LONGER and the cross-correlation between the different communication links needs to be considered separately, causing the computational complexity to be unnecessarily large.' The 2.2/3.7 m medians are the de-correlation of the ZERO-MEAN, offset-subtracted large-scale-fading process; the paper's Figure 10 plots the same link before and after that subtraction and only the subtracted curve decays in 2-3 m. The subtraction is where the antenna gains go -- 'The mean of Psi-sigma has a Gaussian distribution that represents the differences in the particular traffic situation and THE GAIN OF THE INVOLVED ANTENNAS for the particular communication link.'
intersection_measured_decorrelation_dist.licence: CC BY 4.0, verified first-hand on 2026-09-07 from the article's own licence statement. Text/table values, not figure digitisations.
intersection_measured_decorrelation_dist.corrected: 2026-09-07 (RADIO-VS-REALITY.md revision 2, W2). THIS ENTRY AND THE DOCUMENT USED THESE NUMBERS TO CALL THE 10/13 m PIN 'FALSIFIED'. THAT CONCLUSION IS WITHDRAWN. run.py's GeometricChannel has NO antenna-pattern term of any kind (see no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term), so a model of our class sits in this source's 'OTHERWISE' branch -- for which the source PRESCRIBES A LONGER de-correlation distance. Read whole, Nilsson et al. DEFEND the 10/13 m pin for a model without an antenna pattern rather than falsify it. The earlier framing quoted the conditional clause and then drew the conclusion the clause forbids, and it compared our zero-mean AR(1) process against the wrong one of the two curves the source plots side by side.
intersection_measured_decorrelation_dist.note: DISAGREES WITH TR 37.885 AND WITH ETSI TR 103 257-1 in ABSOLUTE VALUE by a factor of ~3-6 (2.2-3.7 m measured vs 10-13 m modelled), BUT THAT COMPARISON CARRIES A NAMED CONFOUND (see conditional_that_governs_these_numbers and the 'corrected' field). WHAT SURVIVES, AND IS THE ACTUAL FINDING, IS IN THE SIBLING ENTRY: Abbas et al. measure urban 4.25/4.5 m and highway 23.3/32.5 m in one campaign under identical processing, so the 5.5-7.2x ENVIRONMENT RATIO is real and confound-free, and our single constant -- keyed on link state only, with no environment term -- cannot express it. The defensible urban statement is '2.35-2.89x longer than Abbas's urban rows'; the earlier '2.2-5.9x' is withdrawn because its sharp end came from these antenna-pattern-corrected intersection medians. See measured_decorrelation_is_environment_dependent and docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md section 2.

measured_decorrelation_is_environment_de.unit: [environment, link state, shadowing decorrelation distance m]
measured_decorrelation_is_environment_de.cite: Abbas, Sjoberg, Karedal & Tufvesson, Int. J. Antennas Propag. 2015, Art. 190607
measured_decorrelation_is_environment_de.source: T. Abbas, K. Sjoberg, J. Karedal and F. Tufvesson, 'A Measurement Based Shadow Fading Model for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Network Simulations', International Journal of Antennas and Propagation, vol. 2015, Article ID 190607, doi:10.1155/2015/190607 (preprint arXiv:1203.3370). MEASURED with the RUSK-LUND channel sounder; verbatim: 'The measurement bandwidth was 200 MHz centered around a carrier frequency of 5.6 GHz'. Data separated into LOS, OLOS (obstructed by vehicles) and NLOS (buildings), in urban and highway scenarios. Table III 'Decorrelation distances dc for highway and urban scenarios': urban 4.25 m LOS / 4.5 m OLOS; highway 23.3 m LOS / 32.5 m OLOS, all four under the same Gudmundson 1/e definition -- 'In the Gudmundson model, dc is defined as the value of delta-d at which the value of the auto-correlation function rx(delta-d) is equal to 1/e'. Table II fitted shadow-fading sigma: 4.15 dB urban LOS / 6.67 dB urban OLOS, 3.95 dB highway LOS / 6.12 dB highway OLOS. The abstract reports that 'vehicles obstructing the LOS induce an additional average attenuation of about 10 dB in the received signal power'. Antenna heights hTX = hRX = 1.47 m.

measured_decorrelation_is_environment_de.note: RECORDED AS A DISAGREEMENT, NOT MERGED. This is the entry that carries the STRUCTURAL finding on decorrelation. TR37885_SHADOW_DECORR_M in run.py is keyed on LINK STATE only ({LOS: 10.0, NLOSv: 13.0, NLOSb: 13.0}) and has no environment term, even though TR37885_PATHLOSS in the same module IS keyed on urban vs highway. These four values come from ONE campaign under IDENTICAL PROCESSING, so the ENVIRONMENT RATIO between them is free of processing confounds: highway/urban is 23.3/4.25 = 5.48x for LOS and 32.5/4.5 = 7.22x for OLOS. NO SINGLE CONSTANT CAN EXPRESS THAT, and our error changes SIGN with radio_env -- 2.35x too long (urban LOS) and 2.89x too long (urban OLOS) against 2.33x and 2.50x too short on highway. READ WITH THE CONFOUND: the ABSOLUTE urban comparison is weakened by our lack of any antenna-pattern term (see no_antenna_gain_or_pattern_term and nlosv_reference_5_13_20_is_model_output); the RATIO is not. Also note the OLOS sigma: 6.12-6.67 dB measured against the 3.0 dB TR 37.885 assigns to NLOSv, i.e. the standard carries roughly half the measured blockage spread. Nothing here changes a model input; see docs/realism/RADIO-VS-REALITY.md sections 2 and 3.

link_state_update_interval_s.source: TR 37.885's evaluation methodology re-evaluates the LOS/NLOSv/NLOS link state at each 100 ms location update ('Link state re-evaluated at each 100 ms location update', docs/realism/investigation/research-net-sota.json section 2(a)); this matches the ETSI CAM 10 Hz upper rate and the MOSAIC 100 ms sync cadence adopted in ROADMAP Phase 1.
link_state_update_interval_s.note: The Python engine's default dt is 1.0 s, i.e. 10x coarser than the standard's update cadence. Reclassifying links once per second is therefore a documented fidelity limitation of the default configuration, not a modelling error; runs at dt <= 0.1 s reproduce the standard's cadence exactly.

nlos_link_budget_consequence_m.unit: [state, EIRP dBm, median range m at -81 dBm sensitivity]
nlos_link_budget_consequence_m.cite: derived: TR 37.885 urban NLOS vs the vendored 802.11p receiver sensitivity
nlos_link_budget_consequence_m.source: Median (zero-shadowing) range at which TR 37.885 urban NLOS path loss equals the link budget EIRP - (-81 dBm), where -81 dBm is the receiver sensitivity configured in the vendored VeReMi-NextGen INET stack (third_party/veremi-nextgen/Generator/docker/scenarios/InTAS_urban_2_4_test/omnetpp/omnetpp.ini:80) and 13.0103 dBm is that stack's 0.02 W transmit power (line 81). Computed at double precision on 2026-08-30; 33 dBm is the ETSI ITS-G5 maximum permitted EIRP.
nlos_link_budget_consequence_m.note: CROSS-CHECK THAT PASSES: at the 33 dBm ETSI ceiling this gives 121.9 m, which independently reproduces the measured 'urban NLoS effective range ~100 m at obstructed intersections' anchor pinned in v2x_awareness.nlos_urban_effective_range_m. Consequence for Phase 2: no realistic power reaches 200 m on an NLOS link, so the '>= 90% awareness at 200 m urban' gate is really a statement about the LOS/NLOSv share of the scenario's link population -- the gate grades the geometry, not the pathloss formula.
